clue.text: Hairdresser punched by Mike Parr? (6)

definitions.note: a parr is a young salmon, so this is a definition by example, flagged by the question mark

indicators.note: something punched has a fist driven into it, so the hairdresser takes the M inside

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A hairdresser gets thumped by a customer called Mike Parr.
explanation.walkthrough: Parr looks like the surname of Mike; it is really the definition, a young salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon in its freshwater stage.

clue.text: Words used to threaten family members in Old English (2,4)

indicators.note: the family members sit in the letters for Old English

explanation.surface: Someone threatens their relatives in the language of Beowulf.
explanation.walkthrough: RELS is crossword shorthand for relations, and OE for Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat left hanging, with the consequence unspoken: the words themselves are the menace.

clue.text: A dash of lemon sorbet ordered with second seafood dish? (8)

definitions.note: singular dish, plural answer: lobsters served as a dish

indicators.note: a dash is a small splash, so only the first letter of lemon
the letters of sorbet are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A restaurant order: lemon sorbet, then a second course of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ordered" sounds like a restaurant order, but it rearranges sorbet; "second" is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the question mark admits these shellfish are one of many seafood dishes.

clue.text: Cryptically, I set WFH (3-4)

blocks.note: warns that the answer is itself a piece of wordplay: its first word is an anagram signal, as in 'off form'
the fodder the answer's instruction acts on, three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter confesses to working from home.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read OFF-SITE as wordplay, OFF says scramble and SITE is the fodder, which gives I SET. The setter is the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Working from home means working off-site, away from the office.

clue.text: Friend captured in war zone where this was used? (6)

definitions.text: Friend captured in war zone where this was used?

indicators.note: the friend is held inside the war zone

explanation.surface: A friend taken prisoner in a war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: Nam is US slang for Vietnam, where napalm was notoriously used, so the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm was used heavily by US forces in Vietnam.

clue.text: Golf celeb formed inclusive large university choir (4,4)

indicators.note: the letters are formed into a new shape

blocks.note: L for large, included in the mix

explanation.surface: A golfing celebrity starts an inclusive university choir.
explanation.walkthrough: "Inclusive" says L and U go into the mix with CELEB before it is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly American: a glee is an unaccompanied part-song, and colleges field clubs to sing them.

clue.text: Fresh quality repair in Esso garages (8)

indicators.note: the clue words house the answer as a garage houses a car

explanation.surface: Esso petrol stations do fresh-looking repair work.
explanation.walkthrough: "Garages" reads as a noun about Esso; as a verb it means houses, and the answer is parked across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a room full of fresh air has that quality, and the noun names it.

clue.text: Tricky over claiming India's opener - 14 for one (6)

definitions.note: 14 is MULLET, and a mullet is one example of a hairdo

indicators.note: the opener of India is its first letter
tricky claims the I, taking it inside

blocks.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A cricket over that tests India's opening batter.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words tempt you to think of a batting side, but India just supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullet (14 Across) is one kind of hairdo.

clue.text: Dortmund miss final, rue getting knocked out (8)

indicators.note: the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Borussia Dortmund miss out on a final and regret being knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: "Miss" looks like a football verb; with Dortmund it is a young German woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fräulein is German for Miss, an unmarried woman, and Dortmund is a German city.

clue.text: Caught a whiff of sulphur (or fish) (6)

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a whiff of sulphur, or perhaps it was fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Smelt is the British past tense of smell; the bracket hides the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: small silvery food fish of the genus Osmerus, whose name is also a verb form.

clue.text: Cuppa served in sober surroundings which uses government money (5,3)

indicators.note: the cuppa is served inside something, so it goes within
the sober word forms the surroundings, the outside layer

blocks.note: a cuppa is a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Tea served in a sober setting, paid for by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: The container is signalled twice, once from each side: the cuppa is served in, the sober word surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: subsidy paid out of the public purse, a term common in EU competition law.

clue.text: Return to grab some attention (8)

blocks.note: a verb: to engage someone's curiosity

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the noun, a return on money; the other is the verb, to hold someone's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the noun is what a bank pays on savings, the verb is catching someone's curiosity.

clue.text: Fox seen in Stroud every now and again (3)

indicators.note: only every other letter turns up

explanation.surface: A fox is spotted occasionally in the Gloucestershire town of Stroud.
explanation.walkthrough: Tod is a dialect word the solver may not know; the even letters of Stroud confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tod is an old Scots and dialect word for a fox.

clue.text: Turn over alien, is it red or grey? (6)

definitions.note: a question whose answer is the fish, which comes as red mullet and grey mullet

blocks.note: to mull over is to turn over in the mind

explanation.surface: Someone flips an alien over to check its colour.
explanation.walkthrough: "Turn over" looks like a reversal instruction but simply means ponder, MULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Red mullet and grey mullet are both fish called mullet.

clue.text: Like a Vogue commercial director's boring angle? (7)

indicators.note: the commercial and director bore into the angle

explanation.surface: A tired camera angle in an ad shot for Vogue magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Vogue is capitalised to suggest the magazine; it is just a fad, and "boring" means drilling, not dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Faddish means like a vogue, following a passing fashion.

clue.text: "Amps not loud" say Glastonbury, happening in the summer (8)

indicators.note: A appears where the loud letter was: A, not F

blocks.note: A is the symbol for amps
f, forte, is loud in music
Glastonbury is an example of a festival

explanation.surface: A complaint that the amps at Glastonbury weren't loud enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glastonbury Festival is a big English music festival held in June; "say" marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Aestival means relating to or occurring in summer.

clue.text: Gladiators failed to put out sea anchor (4,4)

indicators.note: TO is put out of the word
what is left falls apart and re-forms

explanation.surface: Gladiators failed to extinguish something at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: "to" reads as grammar, but it is the letters removed from GLADIATORS.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag sail is a sea anchor, a canvas drogue that slows a drifting vessel.

clue.text: Four year US President which can be a source of irritation (3-4)

explanation.surface: A four-year presidential term that proves irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: "Four year" suggests a presidential term; it is simply IV and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An ivy bush, poison ivy especially, can irritate the skin.

clue.text: Master versus riotous assembly? (8)

indicators.note: the letters of riotous are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A master confronts a riotous crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: "Riotous assembly" reads as one phrase; riotous is the fodder and assembly the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a master of an art, especially music.

clue.text: Compensation sought in NZ for topless dancer's skirt (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, so a topless skirt has lost its T

explanation.surface: Someone in New Zealand seeks damages over a topless dancer's skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Utu is a Maori word, used in New Zealand English, for reciprocity or revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Utu means compensation or payback in New Zealand usage.

clue.text: Domestic nurse consuming unlimited stew provided by her? (7)

definitions.text: Domestic nurse consuming unlimited stew provided by her?
definitions.note: the whole clue describes a caterer

indicators.note: stew loses its limits, the outer letters
the nurse eats the stew, taking it inside

explanation.surface: A home nurse eats stew she made herself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as the definition: someone who provides food like stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer provides food such as stew.

clue.text: Starter of eel, followed by small freshwater fish for Cliff (6)

indicators.note: the starter of eel is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fish supper for Cliff: eel to start, then a little freshwater fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff is capitalised like a name (Cliff Richard, say) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarp, or escarpment, is a steep slope or cliff.

clue.text: Fear Dad being visited by devil incarnate initially (6)

indicators.note: the first letter of incarnate
the visitors go inside Dad

blocks.note: a hob is a hobgoblin, a mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: Dad fears a visit from the devil in person.
explanation.walkthrough: "Devil incarnate" reads as one phrase; the devil is HOB and incarnate gives only its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though stronger: the Greek phobos is fear, and the word now means an irrational dread.

clue.text: A primrose having a golden quality Dulac discovered (8)

indicators.note: Dulac is uncovered, stripped of its outside letters

blocks.note: auric means of or like gold

explanation.surface: The illustrator Edmund Dulac found a flower with a golden sheen.
explanation.walkthrough: "Discovered" means found in the surface, but here it means uncovered: Dulac without its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The auricula is a primrose, Primula auricula, also called bear's ear.

clue.text: Agency address for Ace Skips (4,2)

indicators.note: the letters skip about into a new order

explanation.surface: An agency's address for a firm called Ace Skips, the rubbish-container hire company.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a skip is a large open bin for rubbish, so Ace Skips looks like a firm's name.
explanation.definitionFit: "Care of" (c/o) addresses post through an agent or intermediary.

clue.text: One leaving trail heading north to escort advanced climbers (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north reads the word upwards
the snail walks either side of the A

blocks.note: a snail leaves a slime trail

explanation.surface: A walker heads north on a trail, guiding skilled mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: "Climbers" suggests mountaineers; they are climbing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Lianas are woody climbing vines of tropical forests.

clue.text: Sadly, this family residence sinks in (4,4)

indicators.note: the letters of this end up in a sorry state

explanation.surface: A sad realisation about the family house sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: "Sinks in" looks like subsidence of the house; it means a truth being grasped.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the same thing: a truth that strikes its target is finally understood.

clue.text: Upper-class grandmother describing independent people like Magyars (6)

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so gran goes round the I

explanation.surface: A posh granny sums up the independent Hungarians.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is an old British social label (U and non-U).
explanation.definitionFit: Ugrians are the Ugric-speaking peoples, including the Magyars of Hungary.

clue.text: Travel with Uber-sailor catching 11 fish (4,4)

indicators.note: the sailor catches the 11, holding it inside

blocks.note: an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor on an Uber trip hauls in a catch of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 looks like a reference to 11 Across; here it is just the Roman numeral XI.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling with Uber means taking a taxi ride.

clue.text: East European declaims sluggish carpet cleaner (6)

indicators.note: to declaim is to speak out, so we hear the words

explanation.surface: An East European recites a speech about a sluggish vacuum cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: A vac is British shorthand for a vacuum cleaner; SLOW VAC said aloud is SLOVAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovak is a person from Slovakia in central Europe.
